items.title: Weak Integration has categories but no executable classification contract
items.statement: DL-008 names four Weak Integration categories without defining predicates, precedence, evidence requirements, or the state transition by which an observation becomes first-class Weak Integration. Architecture drift, workflow gap, contract mismatch, and runtime/GUI mismatch can overlap, so different producers can classify the same defect differently.

evidence.exact_quote: Weak integration remains first-class and includes runtime/GUI mismatch,

items.impact: Detection, triage, and closure can drift across runtime, GUI, contracts, workflows, and architecture.
items.builder_discretion: Define deterministic category predicates, overlap rules, and entry/exit states before implementation.

items.title: Weak Integration producers, consumers, and closure oracle are absent
items.statement: The unit does not identify who emits Weak Integration records, which surface consumes them, who owns remediation, or what proof closes them. Its two listed validators establish migration/index conformance, not runtime/GUI, workflow, contract, or architecture agreement.
items.impact: The requirement can remain nominally satisfied while no runtime consumer detects or resolves weak integration.
items.builder_discretion: Specify emitters, owner routing, presentation, acknowledgement, remediation, and falsifiable closure evidence.

items.title: 2-of-3 corroboration does not define eligible or independent inputs
items.statement: DL-009 does not identify the three corroborators, require independence, define freshness or timeout rules, handle abstention and contradictory evidence, or prevent two projections of one source from counting twice. Determinism is asserted without a deterministic input and tie model.

evidence.exact_quote: High-impact claims use deterministic 2-of-3 corroboration, while lesser

items.impact: Correlated, stale, missing, or adversarial inputs can produce a false high-impact decision or indefinite disagreement.
items.builder_discretion: Define source identities, independence, freshness, abstention, contradiction, timeout, and duplicate-source rules.

items.title: Impact classification and advisory visibility lifecycle are undefined
items.statement: No authority or deterministic threshold classifies a claim as high-impact versus lesser, and 'remain visible' has no consumer, retention duration, acknowledgement state, accessibility semantics, localization contract, or rule for promotion when evidence changes.

evidence.exact_quote: unresolved concerns remain visible as non-blocking advisory concerns.

items.impact: Material concerns can be silently downgraded, hidden, inaccessible, or never reconsidered.
items.builder_discretion: Define impact authority, advisory states, audience, expiry, acknowledgement, escalation, and accessible localized presentation.

items.title: Graph generation creation lacks atomicity, race, and rollback semantics
items.statement: DL-010 requires a new generation but omits generation allocation, optimistic concurrency, idempotency, patch conflict handling, partial-write behavior, commit ordering, recovery after interruption, and the rule for selecting the active generation. Two simultaneous patches can fork or overwrite activation state even if lineage rows survive.

evidence.exact_quote: Graph patching creates a new graph generation and preserves superseded

items.impact: Concurrent or interrupted patches can expose a mixed graph, lose the active pointer, or create irreconcilable branches.
items.builder_discretion: Specify atomic commit, version precondition, conflict result, activation ordering, idempotency key, and crash recovery.

items.title: Superseded graph paths are explicitly non-destructive
items.statement: DL-010 explicitly preserves superseded historical paths as visible lineage and prohibits overwriting them without that lineage. This closes the narrow destructive-overwrite ambiguity, although retention and restoration remain open.

evidence.exact_quote: - "Graph patches must not overwrite superseded historical paths without visible lineage."

items.impact: Historical topology is protected from silent destructive replacement.
items.builder_discretion: Implementation may choose storage mechanics if visible lineage remains lossless.

items.title: Source Control and Orchestrator boundary has no handoff contract
items.statement: The ownership slogan does not enumerate commands, statuses, mutations, or deep links that cross between the worktree-first Source Control surface and lane/package/seam Orchestrator context. It also leaves 'compact' undefined and provides no authority rule when both surfaces can initiate a Git-affecting operation.

evidence.exact_quote: Source Control is worktree-first and compact, while Orchestrator carries

items.impact: Callers can duplicate controls, expose conflicting truth, or bypass the intended ownership boundary.
items.builder_discretion: Create an operation-by-operation ownership and navigation matrix with one mutation authority and explicit read models.

items.title: Requested-to-effective runtime identity transition is unspecified
items.statement: DL-012 names requested and effective identity across actors but does not define resolution authority, states, failure results, inheritance, actor handoff, account revocation, concurrent change, or whether a running actor pins or refreshes effective identity.

evidence.exact_quote: Requested/effective runtime identity is shared across assistant, interviewer,

items.impact: Actors may execute under stale, unavailable, or unauthorized identities with no consistent recovery or audit explanation.
items.builder_discretion: Define resolver authority, resolution states, pin/refresh semantics, revocation behavior, handoff propagation, and failure recovery.

items.title: Shared runtime identity lacks privacy and data-lifecycle limits
items.statement: The cross-actor scope does not constrain which identity attributes are shared, persisted, displayed, logged, retained, deleted, or redacted. 'Shared' can therefore expand from a stable reference to provider credentials or personally identifying account metadata.

evidence.exact_quote: - Requested/effective runtime identity spans all named runtime actors.

items.impact: Sensitive identity and provider-account data can leak across actor boundaries or persist beyond purpose.
items.builder_discretion: Specify a minimal shared identity reference, field-level visibility, encryption/redaction, retention, deletion, and audit access.

items.title: Blocked approval identity is not proven unique or replay-safe
items.statement: The tuple does not define the scope and monotonicity of blocked_sequence, whether attempt_id absence is canonicalized, who may mint it, or how duplicate, delayed, and concurrent decisions are rejected. A valid approval for one blocked episode could be replayed against another if tuple allocation or reuse differs by producer.

evidence.exact_quote: Blocked episodes anchored by run_id, node_id, blocked_sequence, and optional

items.impact: Stale or duplicated human decisions can authorize the wrong episode or race with a newer block.
items.builder_discretion: Define tuple uniqueness, sequence scope, minting authority, optional-field canonicalization, compare-and-set decision semantics, and replay rejection.

items.title: Superseding request-centric HITL has no migration or stale-client behavior
items.statement: DL-013 declares a new canonical scope but omits compatibility mapping for stored request IDs, in-flight approvals, older clients, links, receipts, and recovery after a decision races with re-blocking. It does not say whether old identifiers fail closed, redirect, or remain aliases.

evidence.exact_quote: - Request-centric HITL identity is superseded as canonical runtime approval scope.

items.impact: Upgrades can orphan valid approvals, accept stale decisions, or create two canonical identities.
items.builder_discretion: Specify migration, alias lifetime, stale-client error, in-flight conversion, and rollback strategy.

items.title: Navigation primitives lack validation, trust, version, and offline semantics
items.statement: The boundary says which primitive is canonical but not their schemas, origin trust, authorization, encoding, version negotiation, expiry, unknown-target behavior, offline behavior, network-loss recovery, or protection against resume_url injection and unsafe external navigation.

evidence.exact_quote: route_target is the canonical navigation contract, OpenSubject is the

items.impact: Malformed or attacker-controlled navigation can cross authority boundaries, and valid navigation can strand users during version skew or network loss.
items.builder_discretion: Define typed schemas, allowlisted origins/targets, authorization, versioning, safe parsing, expiry, offline fallback, retry, and terminal errors.

items.title: Navigation is classified non-GUI despite user-visible transition obligations
items.statement: DL-014 marks itself non-GUI and supplies no loading, denied, stale, not-found, offline, or partial-navigation presentation; no focus restoration, screen-reader announcement, keyboard continuity, bidirectional-text handling, or localized error contract is attached to the canonical navigation behavior.
items.impact: The runtime contract can be implemented while the UI misleadingly appears idle or successful and excludes assistive-technology and localized users.
items.builder_discretion: Treat navigation outcomes as GUI-related and define visible, accessible, localized transition and failure states.

items.title: Debug capture hygiene lacks enforceable redaction and fail-closed behavior
items.statement: DL-015 prefers allowlisted shapes and structured fields but does not define field-level sensitivity, schema enforcement, nested-value redaction, pre-persistence scanning, untrusted tool output handling, or what happens when redaction, serialization, upload, or storage partially fails. Structured fields can still contain secrets and PII.

evidence.exact_quote: planned for up front, and downstream captures use allowlisted log shapes or

items.impact: Secrets or PII can be persisted or transmitted under an approved field name, especially during failure paths.
items.builder_discretion: Define sensitivity labels, pre-sink enforcement, recursive redaction, untrusted-value limits, fail-closed behavior, and auditable redaction outcomes.

items.title: Debug evidence has no retention, deletion, access, capacity, or support lifecycle
items.statement: The unit omits capture quotas, truncation signaling, backpressure, retention and deletion, legal/privacy holds, viewer authority, export controls, offline buffering, retry deduplication, allowlist evolution, and support-visible diagnostics proving what was omitted or redacted.

evidence.exact_quote: - Secrets in logs, PII, and diff fatigue are planned for up front.

items.impact: Evidence may grow without bound, disappear silently, remain over-retained, or be exposed to unauthorized viewers while support cannot distinguish capture loss from no event.
items.builder_discretion: Specify quotas, truncation markers, buffering/retry, deduplication, retention/deletion, access/export authority, schema migration, and support metrics.

items.title: Validation surfaces do not falsify the runtime decisions
items.statement: Every unit in the window lists only plan-migration and plan-index validators. Those checks do not demonstrate category detection, corroboration independence, graph patch crash safety, surface authority, identity resolution, replay-safe approval, safe navigation, or secret-free capture. The acceptance criteria mostly repeat canonical prose and therefore permit structurally green but behaviorally absent implementations.
items.impact: Governance can report success without executable proof of any required runtime property.
items.builder_discretion: Add unit, integration, property, concurrency, fault-injection, security, accessibility, localization, migration, and end-to-end oracles for the stated contracts.

items.title: Cross-document seams are named but not versioned or owned
items.statement: Implementation surfaces, owner hints, and preserved ContractRef tokens name related documents but do not define producer/consumer direction, schema/version ownership, compatibility window, propagation order, or seam acceptance. The references therefore cannot prevent cross-document semantic drift.
items.impact: Owner documents can each be internally valid while disagreeing at runtime and during migration.
items.builder_discretion: Define seam direction, contract owner, versioning, compatibility, propagation receipts, and end-to-end validation.

items.title: Debug capture explicitly rejects free-form dump capture
items.statement: DL-015 explicitly identifies secrets, PII, and diff fatigue and requires allowlisted shapes or structured fields instead of free-form dumps. This is a meaningful privacy and operability floor, though it is not a complete enforcement or lifecycle contract.
items.impact: The plan rejects the highest-risk unrestricted capture mode.
items.builder_discretion: Choose structured implementation details only within an enforceable allowlist and redaction policy.

dimension_assessments.summary: Weak Integration, advisory concerns, and Source Control-to-Orchestrator handoffs lack explicit producers, consumers, and ownership routing.
Classification, requested-to-effective identity, approval supersession, and navigation transitions lack explicit state machines and invalid-state behavior.
Graph patching, identity changes, blocked approvals, and debug capture retry have no concurrency or deduplication contract.
Mixed graph generations, unresolved identity, interrupted navigation, and failed redaction or capture sinks are unspecified.
No rollback or recovery contract covers graph activation, HITL migration, failed navigation, or interrupted evidence capture.
Cross-surface mutations, identity resolution, approval tuple minting, navigation authorization, and evidence access lack a single authority model.
Runtime identity sharing and debug evidence do not define minimum fields, retention, deletion, redaction, or access lifecycle.
Corroborator evidence, navigation payloads, URLs, and tool/log values lack origin, parsing, validation, and adversarial-input rules.
Visible advisory, lineage, navigation, and runtime/GUI mismatch concepts lack loading, stale, denied, partial, and success truth contracts.
Navigation and evidence capture omit offline behavior, network-loss recovery, retry, and duplicate suppression.
Graph lineage, unresolved advisories, and debug evidence have no retention, pagination, quota, truncation, or backpressure limits.
User-visible advisories, graph lineage, and navigation outcomes have no assistive-technology, focus, keyboard, or announcement semantics.
Advisory and navigation error states lack localization, bidirectional-text, and stable machine-code versus translated-message boundaries.
Request-centric HITL supersession, navigation primitive evolution, identity shape sharing, and referenced document seams lack migration and version-skew rules.
The plan omits decision traces, active-generation diagnostics, identity-resolution explanations, navigation failure codes, and proof of dropped or redacted evidence.
Lineage overwrite is explicitly prohibited, but activation rollback, evidence deletion, retention purge, and redaction replacement remain unspecified.
Named implementation surfaces and ContractRef tokens lack direction, owner, schema, version, propagation, and seam validation.
Only migration/index validation is named; none of the runtime, failure, security, GUI, accessibility, migration, or concurrency claims has an executable oracle.

Undefined terms such as first-class, high-impact, independent corroborator, compact, shared, canonical, visible, and planned up front leave additional implementation-dependent failure modes unbounded.
